doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Musicians who never had it made
summary: Monk recalls Gene Bertoncini playing a wedding and the hidden hardships of sidemen on rock and roll records.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: I used to be quite naïve about my musical heroes and jazz musicians in general thinking that because I saw their names on LPs and in concerts for a long time I assumed that they
sort of “had it made.” Like all they had to do was play jazz gigs and they made a lot of money. And one time I had interviewed Gene Bertoncini, and he happened to mention –
Oh, my boyfriend – I love him. I think he’s almost a hundred and still playing.
The next day he was playing a wedding. And I said, “You’re playing a wedding?” Like I mean I know this stuff because I’m a musician too.
Yeah, right. And Milt Hinton and these fellas who played on these rock & roll records and all that, the story is completely fascinating to me.
